root_cause.text: The fragment queue cleanup path (fqdir_pre_exit) did not flush pending SKBs from the reassembly queues before conntrack's netns exit handler runs, causing conntrack to wait indefinitely for references held by those SKBs and resulting in a deadlock on pernet_ops_rwsem.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "Flush all fragment queue SKBs during fqdir_pre_exit() to release conntrack references before conntrack cleanup runs." The patch adds a loop in fqdir_pre_exit to walk the rhashtable and flush each fragment queue, and also modifies timer expiry handlers to flush when fqdir->dead is set.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description states "Flush all fragment queue SKBs during fqdir_pre_exit() to release conntrack references before conntrack cleanup runs." The patch adds a loop in fqdir_pre_exit to walk the rhashtable and flush each fragment queue, and also modifies timer expiry handlers to flush when fqdir->dead is set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor fqdir_pre_exit from a static inline to a regular function by moving its definition out of the header to a source file.
intent_record.what: Removed the static inline definition of fqdir_pre_exit and replaced it with a function declaration (prototype) in the header file.
intent_record.how: The function is no longer defined inline in the header; its implementation is moved to a separate source file. At runtime, the function will be called as a regular function instead of being inlined at every call site.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature exit from ip6frag_expire_frag_queue when fqdir is dead to ensure proper locking and processing, fixing a potential bug.
intent_record.what: Removed a check for fqdir->dead flag and the associated comment, which previously caused an early return from ip6frag_expire_frag_queue before acquiring the spin lock.
intent_record.how: The function no longer exits early when fqdir is dead; it will always acquire the spin lock and proceed with fragment queue expiration processing even if fqdir is marked dead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a race condition in ip6frag_expire_frag_queue by checking if the fqdir is dead before accessing network device structures.
intent_record.what: Add a check for fq->q.fqdir->dead after inet_frag_kill; if dead, call inet_frag_queue_flush and jump to out.
intent_record.how: During fragment queue expiration, if the fqdir is marked dead (via READ_ONCE), the queue is flushed and the function exits early, preventing access to potentially freed resources.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add fqdir_pre_exit to flush incomplete fragment queues before fqdir exit to prevent memory leaks and ensure proper cleanup.
intent_record.what: Added a new function fqdir_pre_exit that sets fqdir->high_thresh to 0 and fqdir->dead to true, then walks the rhashtable and flushes any incomplete fragment queues by calling inet_frag_queue_flush for each non-complete queue.
intent_record.how: This function prevents new fragment queue creation by zeroing high_thresh, marks the fqdir as dead to block further operations, and drains all existing incomplete queues before the subsequent fqdir_exit, ensuring no pending fragments remain during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against an uninitialized (zero) drop reason by defaulting to FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT in fragment queue flush.
intent_record.what: Added a default assignment for the `reason` variable in `inet_frag_queue_flush` such that if it is zero, it is set to `SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT`.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that `inet_frag_rbtree_purge` always receives a non-zero drop reason, preventing potential issues with uninitialized or zero reason codes when flushing fragment queues, particularly in timeout scenarios.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature exit in ip_expire when fqdir is dead to correct fragment expiration behavior and avoid missing necessary cleanup.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional check that caused early exit from ip_expire when qp->q.fqdir->dead is true, including the associated comment about pairing with WRITE_ONCE in fqdir_pre_exit().
intent_record.how: Without this guard, ip_expire will no longer bypass its processing when the fqdir is marked dead; instead, it proceeds to acquire the spinlock and handle the fragment queue normally, which may affect whether expired fragments are properly cleaned up or not.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix race condition in ip_expire by checking fqdir->dead and flushing queue early during netns teardown.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block in ip_expire() that reads fqdir->dead with READ_ONCE and, if true, calls inet_frag_queue_flush() and jumps to 'out', bypassing subsequent stats updates.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the fqdir is marked dead (netns exit), the function flushes the fragment queue and skips incrementing IPSTATS_MIB_REASMFAILS and REASMTIMEOUT, preventing use-after-free and incorrect statistics.

Fix race condition in ip_expire by checking fqdir->dead and flushing queue early during netns teardown.
Remove premature exit in ip_expire when fqdir is dead to correct fragment expiration behavior and avoid missing necessary cleanup.
Guard against an uninitialized (zero) drop reason by defaulting to FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT in fragment queue flush.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix race conditions in IP fragment expiration during network namespace teardown by properly handling the fqdir->dead flag, including removing incorrect premature exits and adding appropriate checks before accessing network device structures.
Fix fragment expiration and cleanup around fqdir exit by adding pre-exit flush and removing premature exit in ip_expire.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address race conditions and proper handling of fqdir->dead flag during netns teardown, which is the core issue in the vulnerability where fragment queue cleanup did not flush SKBs before conntrack exit, causing a deadlock.

The group adds fqdir_pre_exit to flush incomplete fragment queues before fqdir exit, which directly addresses the root cause of the deadlock by ensuring cleanup occurs before conntrack's netns exit handler runs. Removing the premature exit in ip_expire also corrects expiration behavior to avoid missing necessary cleanup.

The group addresses an uninitialized drop reason default, which is a minor code quality improvement. It does not directly address the deadlock caused by flushing SKBs before conntrack's netns exit handler.

Causes early return from ip6frag_expire_frag_queue when fqdir is dead, skipping the necessary processing that would release SKB references and unblock conntrack's netns exit handler.
